messages:
sarah: We saw repeated GPU cost when clients abort streaming responses mid-gen. Retry/hedge paths replay the entire generation, doubling GPU time. Proposing split control vs payload streams at the edge so we can ack/hold without occupying a model slot. Thoughts?
rashid: Sounds promising. Can you sketch protocol? Is this multiplexing over same conn or separate connections? :thinking_face:
sarah: Multiplex over same TCP conn initially. Control channel is low-bandwidth for admission, policy, resume tokens. Payload channel carries token deltas. Key idea: on abort we return a resume_token instead of immediately queuing work.
marta: How do we ensure deterministic resume? Sampling makes resumed runs diverge. Options: require client seed, only allow resume for greedy/beam, or capture RNG+KV state checkpoint.
sarah: Agreed. Proposal: resume is allowed when client provided seed or model set deterministic. Otherwise we can keep lightweight KV cache checkpoints for short TTL to rehydrate without replaying full history.
lucas: KV cache checkpoints are memory-heavy. Need budget and eviction policy. Maybe checkpoint only every K tokens or only prefixes under length L. Also compress checkpoints.
rashid: Also need sequence semantics for payload fragments. If control ack happens before payload arrives, clients might interleave fragments. Add frag_id and resume_offset headers. Keep simple: frag_id monotonic per-session; resume_offset byte token index.
infra-bot: infra: noted. Storage impact estimate request: projected checkpoint retention per 100k sessions = X GB. Please attach numbers.
sarah: Will run load sim and post results. Quick sketch of control proto (pseudo):
```
CONTROL -> { action: admit|defer|reject, resume_token: "...", ttl: 60 }
PAYLOAD -> { frag_id: 12, offset: 384, tokens: "..." }
```
Edge behavior:
- on admit: issue 202 and optional resume_token, do not allocate GPU until model slot assigned
- on defer: enqueue but keep lightweight checkpoint
- on client abort: keep checkpoint for ttl, allow client to resume using token within ttl
Tradeoffs:
- pros: reduces wasted GPU time, better cost accounting
- cons: added complexity in edge, state retention, determinism constraints
marta: Also consider API ergonomics. Clients should get explicit enum for resume capability and failure reasons (expired, nondeterministic). Add http header X-Resume-Capable: yes|no.
devex: We should publish a client library patch that handles resume tokens and sequence reassembly. Also add console metrics: resumed_count, resume_fails, checkpoint_mem_used.
sarah: Good. Next steps: I'll prototype control/payload mux, run sim to estimate checkpoint mem and hit rates. If numbers look good, write an RFC with more formal protocol text and opt-in feature flag for hosted users.
lucas: One more: failure modes. If edge loses checkpoint, must surface explicit 410 and instruct client to retry from scratch. Also think about audit/logging of resume tokens (don't log sensitive payloads).
sarah: Agreed. I'll include rotateable token signing and short TTL. Thanks all :thumbsup:
